title: Specific performance and adequacy of damages
shortTitle: Specific performance and adequacy of damages
summary: Specific performance directs promised performance where money is inadequate to protect the relevant interest.
notes: Morris uses the particular trained horse’s value to the plaintiff. The notes extend the inquiry to affection for a pet and the inability to obtain sufficient tomatoes at the needed time for a cannery. Uniqueness is relevant through difficulty of substitution, not only through a category label. Personal services present different concerns; a negative injunction against competing performance is distinct from an affirmative order to render services.
